pages	pages/about.html	Civgraph is a home for the digitising, scanning and research of volunteer contributors to coexist alongside the original sources, always clearly distinguished from them. Many of our maps are scanned and digitised by our volunteers where no official digitised version existed, mirrored and backed up for the years to come, and made available in full.

pages	index.html	The 1984 council wards - 552 boundaries, hand-digitised in QGIS for Civgraph because no digital version existed. The date slider sets the map to 1984, and the panel lists the same geography at 1972, 1993, 2012 and 2023.
pages	pages/about.html	The 1984 council wards, the map Civgraph began with. No digital version existed, so its wards were digitised in QGIS from OSNI scans and townland geometry.
pages	pages/about.html	The 1984 ward map took months of evenings this way. The same method has since been applied to Republic of Ireland electoral divisions, and it is the work we most need help with. Alongside it we scan books from libraries: first boundary commissioners' reports explaining why boundaries were drawn where they were, then other volumes that weren't online and could legally be scanned and redistributed.

pages	pages/about.html	The obstacle to using any of it together is that the boundaries move.
